ai.description: *Gegeneophis goaensis* is a slender caecilian reaching 25 cm. It is uniform dark brown with a paler snout and possesses distinct primary annuli, lacking secondary grooves or a tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis goaensis* is distinguished from other Indian caecilians by its unique combination of having no secondary annuli and possessing a distinct, pale-colored snout.
ai.habitat: The Goa caecilian inhabits moist, tropical evergreen forests and agricultural plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 100 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Goa Caecilian is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through moist soil to forage for earthworms and other small subterranean invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis goaensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 10–18 eggs in underground nests during the monsoon season (June–August). The female provides maternal care.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis goaensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in the Indian states of Goa and Maharashtra, typically found at elevations between 100 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Goa Caecilian produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of clicks or chirps, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter near stream banks.
